$comment: The behaviour id registry (#71, FR-007). The single source that scripts/floor-reporter.mjs,
mutations.json and the conformance matrix all read. Tests are keyed by ID, never by title,
so renaming a test does not silently drop coverage or break the mutation harness.

FIFTEEN entries, fourteen of them APPLICABLE. The fifteenth is generation determinism (SC-023), declared with applicable:false and the gate that discharges it named on the entry. It was deferred while the wrapper generator did not exist; #126 built the generator and its --check gate, and #75 WP04 settled it.

A behaviour with no applicable subject is either ABSENT from this file, or DECLARED with applicable:false and an inapplicableReason naming the gate that discharges it. It is never expressed as a skip and never deferred to a matrix cell — that was FR-010's earlier shape and it made the mission incoherent if the conformance matrix were dropped.

The second form is for a behaviour ADR-11 states as a CI-gate obligation rather than a runtime one: it has no test to mutate, but omitting it would leave the registry silently short of the ADR's list. #75 WP04 added the first, SC-023. Declaring one is not an escape hatch — config-contract asserts the applicable set equals ADR-11's list exactly, so nothing can be demoted to dodge a mutation, and it asserts the inapplicable set exactly too.
SUBJECTS (#73, FR-010). A behaviour id is no longer unique across the suite: sk-nav-pill
carries SC-006..SC-010 and SC-012, and the synthetic fixture carries them too. An id-only
coverage check therefore stayed GREEN with the ELEMENT's entire behaviour file deleted,
because the fixture still covered every id. That is this programme's certifying-absence
class, inside the reporter written to catch it.
Each subject names the FILE that must carry the id. scripts/floor-reporter.mjs checks
coverage per (id, subject file); scripts/suite-selftest.mjs's guard 7 compares mutations
against the same pairs, and a mutation's optional `subject` narrows which file's named
test it must red.
A subject's `name` is what tests/node/config-contract.test.ts matches against the ELEMENT
glob, so it names the element (sk-stub, sk-card, sk-nav-pill), not the test file's role. A
lens added a real element with no entry here and every gate went green — this registry was
the last hand-maintained list deciding whether an element is tested at all.
SC-002..SC-005 finally have a REAL subject (#74). They were written in #71 for this mission
and until now were carried only by the synthetic fixture — which is why the id-only coverage
check could not tell 'the fixture covers form association' from 'a shipped element does'.

#77 adds <sk-grid> as a subject of SC-013 and SC-014 — the two it genuinely owns. It is deliberately NOT added to SC-015: the registry guard is a claim about define(), not about any element that calls it, and listing every caller would make the id's subject list grow without adding an assertion.

#77 adds <sk-section-banner> as a subject of SC-013 and SC-014 on the same basis as <sk-grid>: it declares parts and adopts a generated sheet. It does not join SC-015, and does not claim an event or form id it does not have.

#78 adds <sk-feature-card> AND <sk-ribbon-card> as subjects of SC-013 and SC-014, on the same basis as #77's two: each declares parts and adopts a generated sheet. An earlier revision of this note named only feature-card while the data below added both.

#79 adds sk-button, sk-pill-tag and sk-check-bullet to SC-013 and SC-014. None claims an event or form id: button renders a real control and lets the platform supply the behaviour, and the other two are presentational.

#78 adds <sk-blog-card> to SC-013 and SC-014. Its SC-014 case is the only one in the repo that asserts TWO adopted sheets by identity and in order — the operator ruling has it compose sk-card's stylesheet rather than nest the element, so 'adopts the generated sheet' becomes 'adopts both, sk-card's first'.

#77 adds sk-site-footer to SC-013 and SC-014. Declaring the subject is what CREATES the obligation — nothing detects that a new element should have behaviour tests, and the suite's own floor proved it: with the tests written and passing but no subject declared, the run failed with '<sk-site-footer> exists but is not a subject of any behaviour ... it would ship with zero behaviour tests and every gate green'. That is the gate working.

#146 WP01 adds section-header to SC-013/SC-014 and adds status-indicator and entity-marker to SC-010/SC-013/SC-014. Slot projection and accessible naming remain direct assertions rather than mislabeled behavior ids.

#146 WP02 adds sk-action-row to SC-006/SC-007/SC-008/SC-010/SC-013/SC-014. SC-009 is intentionally absent because its activation request is non-cancelable and the component owns no preventable default action.
#146 WP03 adds react-action-row only to SC-006: its generated wrapper must deliver the action request once without changing the exact event or frozen detail identity.

#177 adds sk-card to SC-010. It was already an SC-013 subject and stays one; SC-010 is NEW to it because `status` is its first reflected STRING property — `variant` predates the id's adoption here and `inset` is boolean. Declaring the subject is what creates the obligation, per sk-site-footer's note above. sk-card is deliberately NOT added to SC-014: it adopts a generated sheet, but the claim there is asserted for it indirectly by sk-blog-card, whose two-sheet identity case imports sk-card's sheet by name, and adding a duplicate subject would grow the registry without adding an assertion. #177 also does not mint an id for fail-open: that behaviour is carried by SC-013, honestly rather than by relabelling, because a throw inside render() blanks the shadow root and the declared ::part() literally stops being targetable.

#147 WP03 records sk-metric and sk-evidence-chain as SC-013 subjects. Their approved WP01/WP02 fixture files already target every declared part; the shared registry is recorded here because config-contract derives every element and refuses an unregistered subject. No new behaviour id or SC-014 claim is added.

behaviours.summary: native form submit produces the expected FormData entry
setValidity blocks submission and the message reaches the a11y tree
form reset restores the initial value
a disabled control is excluded from submission
a property assigned before the definition loads is applied on upgrade
content reaches the intended slot; fallback appears when empty
Escape closes, focus returns to the invoker, aria-expanded tracks state
every declared ::part() is present and targetable from outside
behaviours.note: Subject-owned. Shipped elements declare styling hooks with @csspart and render matching part= surfaces; expected-parts.json rejects manifest drift, while every registered subject fixture proves its declared parts are present and externally targetable. The synthetic fixture remains as harness self-coverage.

behaviours.summary: adopts a constructed stylesheet by identity and injects no <style> element
a second define warns, keeps the original constructor, and is silent for the same constructor
regenerating wrappers from an unchanged manifest is a no-op, and drift fails CI
behaviours.inapplicableReason: ADR-11 item 9 assigns this to the NODE lane and states it as two clauses: regeneration is a no-op, AND drift fails CI. Both are enforced by scripts/build-react-wrappers.mjs --check, which generates twice and compares byte-for-byte before comparing against the committed tree, as an ENFORCED lint-code step with two REQUIRED_LINT entries. It is not a mutation-harness behaviour: suite-selftest.mjs runs the browser project only, and extending it to the node lane would add ~1.8s to each of 44 runs (~240s against a 180s ceiling) to re-prove what a --check gate already proves. Declared here rather than omitted so the registry mirrors ADR-11's fifteen and the discharge is recorded where a reader looks.
